question.text: A large glass slab $\left(\mu=\frac{5}{3}\right)$ of thickness 8 $\mathrm{cm}$ is placed over a point source of light on a plane surface. It is seen that light emerges out of the top surface of the slab from a circular area of radius $R \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the value of $R$ ?

solution.text: $$ \frac{R}{t}=\tan \theta_C $$ or $\quad R=t\left(\tan \theta_C\right)$ $$ \begin{aligned} & \text { But, } \quad \sin \theta_C=\frac{1}{\mu}=\frac{3}{5} \\ & \therefore \quad \tan \theta_C=\frac{3}{4} \\ & \therefore \quad R=\frac{3}{4} t=\frac{3}{4}(8 \mathrm{~cm})=6 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \end{aligned} $$ Hence the answer is 6 .
